hero.headline: Hurricane, Utah Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Plan a focused Hurricane trip with practical highlights, local context, and easy tour connections.

overview: Hurricane sits in Washington County between Zion approaches, sandstone mesas, and desert trail systems.
The city is a base for OHV riding, canyon stops, and day trips across southern Utah's red-rock corridor.

highlights.title: Hurricane essentials
highlights.description: Prioritize one signature attraction each day for better pacing.

highlights.title: Hurricane local character
highlights.description: Add nearby neighborhoods and outdoor stops for variety.

thingsToDo.title: Sand Mountain
thingsToDo.description: Sand Mountain is a large dune and sandstone riding area on the edge of Hurricane. The site is known for OHV routes, steep climbs, and broad desert views.

thingsToDo.title: One Day
thingsToDo.description: One Day Canyon is a short slot-canyon route near Hurricane with narrow passages and layered sandstone walls. It is a compact technical hike in the region's dry desert terrain.

thingsToDo.title: Toquerville Falls
thingsToDo.description: Toquerville Falls is a desert waterfall and swimming hole reached by backcountry road north of Hurricane. Basalt ledges and red-rock canyon walls define the setting.

thingsToDo.title: Flintstone House
thingsToDo.description: Flintstone House is a dome-style residence in the Hurricane area known for unconventional concrete architecture. Its rounded forms stand out against the surrounding desert landscape.

thingsToDo.title: West Rim
thingsToDo.description: West Rim marks Zion's high plateau zone west of the main canyon and is accessible from the Hurricane region. The terrain includes forested sections, exposed rims, and long elevation views.

thingsToDo.title: Warner Valley
thingsToDo.description: Warner Valley is an open desert basin south of Hurricane with volcanic features, dirt roads, and remote trail access. The area links backcountry routes toward dinosaur tracks and regional preserves.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Shoulder seasons are typically easiest in Hurricane
bullets: Spring and fall usually offer comfortable weather and smoother logistics.
Reserve popular tours and timed attractions early in busy periods.
Use morning starts for major sights and photo-heavy locations.

travelTips: Group activities by area to reduce transfers across Hurricane.
Pre-book top tours and high-demand attractions when your dates are set.
Leave one flexible time block each day for weather and local recommendations.

faq.q: How many days should I plan for Hurricane?
faq.a: Two to three days is enough for core Hurricane highlights plus one or two local experiences.

faq.q: Should I book tours ahead in Hurricane?
faq.a: Yes—advance booking is recommended for weekends, holidays, and top-rated operators.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Hurricane is a small desert city east of St. George with direct access to regional trail and canyon networks.

sections.heading: Geography & setting
paragraphs: It lies on a bench above the Virgin River valley near sandstone formations, lava fields, and open desert.

sections.heading: History (brief)
paragraphs: Hurricane began as an agricultural settlement and now functions as a service center for outdoor recreation in Washington County.

sections.heading: Culture & neighborhoods
paragraphs: The city combines a traditional main-street core with newer residential growth along highway corridors.

sections.heading: Outdoor & seasonal highlights
paragraphs: Spring and fall offer the most consistent conditions for off-road routes, hiking, and nearby water-based stops.

sections.heading: Getting around
paragraphs: Most major sites around Hurricane are dispersed, and road travel is standard between trailheads and scenic areas.
